subject: french
title: Stamp 2: The Resistance
welcome_lead: Stamp the French Resistance and de Gaulle's London call.
meta_desc: A-Level French adventure on La Resistance, de Gaulle's 18 June 1940 appeal, and liberation.

concepts.def: Movements fighting Vichy and the German occupier, both in France and abroad.
De Gaulle's BBC broadcast on 18 June 1940 calling on French to continue fighting.
Free French Forces organised in London by de Gaulle from 1940.
Resistance leader who unified networks; arrested and tortured to death in 1943.
Rural Resistance groups hiding in remote areas, especially after 1942-43.
Allied advance through France in summer 1944, culminating in liberation of Paris 25 August.

walkthroughs.body_html: From London on 18 June 1940, de Gaulle declared via BBC: 'La France a perdu une bataille! Mais la France n'a pas perdu la guerre!' The speech is foundational to Resistance mythology.
Networks like Liberation, Combat, and Franc-Tireur emerged separately. Jean Moulin unified them into the Conseil national de la Resistance in May 1943, just before his arrest by Klaus Barbie.
D-Day: 6 June 1944 in Normandy. Provence landings: 15 August 1944. Liberation of Paris: 25 August 1944. De Gaulle entered the city and walked down the Champs-Elysees.
